title: Constant finite-projective models and evaluated diagram projections
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $u:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ be a morphism of topoi presented by small sites, with the canonical identification $u^{-1}\underline A_{\mathscr Y}\cong\underline A_{\mathscr X}$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $(B_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative $A$-algebras with unital $A$-algebra transitions [def-weil-inverse-system]. Assume each underlying $A$-module $B_n[0]$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Write $c_T$ for exact termwise constant realization on $T=\mathscr X,\mathscr Y$ [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$, and $\Delta_T$ for constant towers, using the diagram sites [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Put
$$\mathcal B_T(F)=\Delta_TF\otimes^L_{\Delta_T\underline A_T}(\underline{B_n}_T)_n.$$
Let $P=Ru_*$ and $Q=Ru_*^{\mathcal T}$, and use the normalized constant-tower comparison $\chi_F:\Delta_{\mathscr Y}PF\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\Delta_{\mathscr X}F$ [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization]. Define $h_F:\mathcal B_{\mathscr Y}(PF)\to Q\mathcal B_{\mathscr X}(F)$ to be the diagram-site projection adjoint to counit tensored with identity, with source identified through $\chi_F$ [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate].
For each $n$, any chosen bounded complex $E_n^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules representing $B_n[0]$ gives a bounded representative $c_T(E_n^\bullet)$ of $\underline{B_n}_T[0]$. If $E_n^r\xrightarrow{s_{n,r}}A^{m_{n,r}}\xrightarrow{p_{n,r}}E_n^r$ are finite-free splitting maps with $p_{n,r}s_{n,r}=1$, their constant realizations, under $c_T(A^{m_{n,r}})\cong\underline A_T^{m_{n,r}}$, satisfy the same identity. Thus they give a strict-perfect coefficient package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] representing that constant coefficient. Under canonical evaluation/direct-image and tensor comparisons, for every unbounded $F\in D(\mathscr X,\underline A)$,
$$\operatorname{ev}_n(h_F)=\pi_{u,F,\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}}:(PF)\otimes^L\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}\longrightarrow P(F\otimes^L\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr X}),$$
where $\pi$ is the canonical counit-tensor projection of [lem-sbc-ringed-site-perfect-projection-formula]; this specified evaluated morphism is invertible, naturally in $F$. The representatives and splittings may be chosen independently for different $n$: no chain-level lifts of coefficient transitions and no common bound on their lengths or ranks are required.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and any bounded finite-projective representative $E_n^\bullet$ with an isomorphism $E_n^\bullet\simeq B_n[0]$ in $D(A)$; such representatives exist by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. In each nonzero degree take finite generators of $E_n^r$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], giving a surjection $p_{n,r}:A^{m_{n,r}}\to E_n^r$. The lifting characterization of projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], applied to $1_{E_n^r}$ and this surjection, gives $s_{n,r}$ with $p_{n,r}s_{n,r}=1$. Outside the finite interval use the zero module and rank zero. This constructs precisely degreewise splittings, without imposing any equation between splittings and differentials.

proof.text: For $T=\mathscr X,\mathscr Y$, constant module realization is the sheafification of constant module presheaves and acts on maps by sheafifying the same linear map [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. The presheaf $A^m$ is the finite product of $m$ copies of the constant presheaf $A$. Finite-product preservation of sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] identifies $c_T(A^m)$ with $\underline A_T^m$, including $m=0$; the projections and scalar actions are the sheafifications of the coordinate maps, so this is an isomorphism of module sheaves. Functoriality gives $c_T(p_{n,r})c_T(s_{n,r})=c_T(1)=1$. Hence each $c_T(E_n^r)$ is a finite-free retract. These maps are the data of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]; their idempotent equations follow by composing this splitting identity. No claim that these terms are projective objects of the sheaf category is used.

By [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], the exact additive constant module functor descends to $D(A)$ with its termwise representative comparison. Apply this functor to the chosen isomorphism $E_n^\bullet\simeq B_n[0]$. Its two images are represented by $c_T(E_n^\bullet)$ and $\underline{B_n}_T[0]$, respectively, and the image is an isomorphism. Additivity preserves zero terms and the equation $d^{r+1}d^r=0$, so $c_T(E_n^\bullet)$ has the same finite degree interval. Together with Step 2 this is a bounded finite-free-retract representative, hence a perfect coefficient object in the exact sense of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. The argument works for every chosen representative, not merely a particular resolution.

Use the canonical constant-ring identification in the hypothesis. For this geometric morphism, [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] makes module pullback $u_A^*$ exact. By [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module], for every $A$-module $M$ there is the canonical natural isomorphism $u_A^*\underline M_{\mathscr Y}\cong\underline M_{\mathscr X}$. Apply it to $M=B_n$ and to every transition $B_{n+1}\to B_n$. The comparisons carry constant elements to the same constant elements, so they respect multiplication and unit as well: locally all coefficient sections are constant, and on two constant sections both sides send $(b,b')$ to $bb'$, and send $1$ to $1$. Thus the tower $Q_{Y,\bullet}=(\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y})_n$ pulls back to precisely $(\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr X})_n$ as a tower of algebra sheaves with its given transitions. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], this exact pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms and is computed termwise. To compare with the derived pullback $Lu^*$ of the projection formula, choose a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}[0]$ with $P$ K-flat with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], $\epsilon_P\circ Lu^*(p)^{-1}$ identifies $Lu^*(\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}[0])$ with $u^*P$, where $u^*$ is $u_A^*$ under the ring identification. Exactness makes $u_A^*(p)$ a quasi-isomorphism, so $Lu^*(\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}[0])\cong\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr X}[0]$, compatibly with transitions by naturality in resolutions.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate] with $f=u$, $R_T=\underline A_T$, the algebra tower of Step 4, and $K=F$. The explicit formula in [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower] identifies its reduction $B_T(K)$ with $\mathcal B_T(K)$, and its source identification is exactly the $\chi_F$ specified in the item. It therefore constructs this same morphism $h_F$, not just a morphism between isomorphic objects. The normalized constant comparison [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization] evaluates to the identity. The evaluated-mate clause then says that, under the canonical tensor and direct-image comparisons, $\operatorname{ev}_n(h_F)$ is the counit-tensor morphism $PF\otimes^L\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}\to P(F\otimes^L\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr X})$. Under Step 4's pullback identification, this is precisely $\pi_{u,F,\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}}$: both are adjuncts of the canonical pullback-tensor comparison followed by $\varepsilon_F\otimes1$, with the same counit. The augmented-mate statement also supplies naturality in $F$.

proof.text: For every fixed $n$, Step 3 makes $\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}[0]$ perfect. Apply [lem-sbc-ringed-site-perfect-projection-formula] to the original ringed-topos morphism $u$, $E=F$ and $P=\underline{B_n}_{\mathscr Y}[0]$. Its hypotheses require only a perfect coefficient object and allow arbitrary unbounded $F$; the sites are small and the coefficient rings are commutative as assumed. It follows that the specified map in Step 5 is invertible. Its naturality in $F$ is the naturality of the counit-tensor projection [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Thus this is the claimed natural isomorphism, with the stipulated map as forward arrow.

The tower morphism used above was constructed from the actual algebra transitions before any choices of $E_n^\bullet$ or degreewise splittings. The choices in Steps 1--3 only verify the perfectness hypothesis separately for each evaluation in Step 6. No map between chosen complexes at different indices is used in any step, and only the finite interval for the single fixed $n$ enters that application. Therefore the representatives and splittings can be chosen independently at all indices, with no common bound on interval lengths or finite ranks.
